messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: runtime OOM observed on pool-prod-gpu-7. Severity: P1. Affected route: /v1/generate (latency spikes, 5xx). Logs uploaded to /shared/incident/3162240000/logs.zip
Alice M.: I'm on it. Pulling logs now. Can someone grab recent nvml + runtime memstat?
Bhanu R.: grabbing nvml from node gpu-7, also pulling kvcache stats. Pasting quick dump:
```
# nvml-summary
GPU 0: total=40GB, used=39.2GB, free=0.8GB
processes: python[redwood_runtime] pid=2211 mem=34.6GB
page-in: 1.2GB/s (last 5m)
page-out: 600MB/s
```
```
# kvcache-stats
kv_total_entries: 3.2M
kv_eviction_rate: 18% (last 10m)
kv_swap_reads: 42/s
avg_kv_entry_size: 540 bytes
```
Carl S.: thanks. I also see repeated allocation failures in the runtime logs around 3162240018: `malloc failed: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation` then a cascade of batch retries.
Dana L.: Customer impact: a subset of requests got 500s between 3162240020-3162240125. CS reported one customer (acme-inc) complaining about timeouts. Not yet widespread but sustained for ~2 minutes.
Alice M.: Hypothesis A: KV cache churn + large batch boundary caused transient fragmentation -> allocation failures. Hypothesis B: sudden spike in long-context requests bumped sequence lengths and pushed memory over threshold.
Bhanu R.: timeline I compiled:
- 3162240000 alert fired (OOM signaled)
- 3162240005 spike in 1024+ token requests (per gateway logs)
- 3162240012 first cuda alloc failure observed
- 3162240018 batch retry loop begins (backoff)
- 3162240030 page-in rate peaks
- 3162240125 errors subside after autoscaler evict/trim event
Actions taken live: reduced default batch_size from 16 -> 8 at 3162240024, triggered kvcache-trim at 3162240028 via ops-bot.
ops-bot: Executed command `redwoodctl pool trim-kv --pool pool-prod-gpu-7 --ratio 0.25` at 3162240028. Result: trimmed 820k entries.
Carl S.: Can we correlate which model variants were serving? Looks like v2.11 quantized-8bit. That variant keeps larger local KV indices per shard.
Dana L.: CS: acme-inc reports 37 failed calls. They've been notified we’re investigating; offering postmortem.
Alice M.: Quick mitigation suggestions (short-term):
- keep batch_size=8 for 30m
- enable aggressive kv trim policy (0.3) during window
- add fallback to cpu-small for very long contexts (>1500 tokens)
Bhanu R.: I'm attaching a small log excerpt that shows batch sizes and sequence lengths:
```
[3162240010] req_id=abc123 seq_len=128 batch=12
[3162240010] req_id=def456 seq_len=1536 batch=4
[3162240012] cuda alloc fail on 183MB block
[3162240013] retrying request def456 as batch=1
```
Alice M.: Good catch — mixed short+very-long requests in same batch is a risk. We should consider batching by token-length buckets, not just arrival time. Queueing tweak ticket?
Carl S.: I can spin a canary flag to enforce length-bucketed batching on the pool for a 1-hour trial. Will need a config: `batching.strategy=length_bucket` and bucket thresholds.
Dana L.: I'll take ownership for customer comms: update acme-inc with timeline + short-term mitigations.
Bhanu R.: Post-incident data to collect for RCA: full nvml traces, runtime heapmaps, per-request token counts, kvcache eviction logs, and scheduler trace. I'll upload to /shared/incident/3162240000/trace/ by EOD.
Alice M.: Next steps:
- Bhanu: collect traces and synthesize mem histograms (ETA 2h)
- Carl: enable length-bucketed canary on pool (ETA 10m)
- Dana: customer comms (immediate)
- Ops: maintain batch_size=8 + kv trim policy for 30m
Anyone else?
Carl S.: Starting canary now. Will post results.
ops-bot: set pool batch_size=8 on pool-prod-gpu-7 at 3162240024.
Alice M.: Logging this thread into the incident timeline. Marking action items in the incident tracker. If I hand off to next oncall, I will ensure traces link included.
Bhanu R.: Uploaded traces: /shared/incident/3162240000/trace/{nvml.log,heapmap.pb,kv_eviction.log,scheduler.trace}
Alice M.: Handing off to @Carl S. at 3162240365 — I'm stepping out for meeting. Please continue RCA and update timeline.
Carl S.: Ack, taking over. I will run binary search on bucket thresholds and report back.
Dana L.: I'll update CS with ETA for RCA (4-6 hours) and note our mitigations. :white_check_mark:
